evidence_standard: An entry is `platform` (or `flow_controller`, the same bar for code that sequences a flow's stages at runtime) only when a real handler is named at file and symbol AND an EXECUTABLE test drives it in both directions — the refusal fires, and a legitimate control is allowed. Three forms of test are accepted, and nothing else is: (1) a live chain-check probe under `packages/tools/src/testing/` that CALLS the tool over its real door and asserts both the refusal and a successful control — the strongest form, run by `scripts/release.ts` against a live deployment; (2) a check under `checks/` that imports the compiled module and drives the enforcing predicate the handler calls, where the handler's call site is cited at file:line so the predicate is demonstrably not an orphan; (3) a check under `checks/` that lifts the handler's own refusal conditions out of its comment-stripped source and EVALUATES them over every combination of the inputs. A check that regexes source text, an export that exists, and a unit test over a subsystem nothing else imports satisfy none of these. `analytical_review` is used where a real handler enforces the claim but NO executable test of any of the three forms drives it — the handler is still named, so the gap is visible rather than hidden, and the entry is promoted to `platform` the day a test drives it. `convention` is used where nothing executable enforces the claim at all.

enforcement_classes.platform: Refused by the platform's own code, and a check drives that refusal in both directions.
enforcement_classes.flow_controller: Computed by the platform's flow machinery at runtime, and a check drives it in both directions.
enforcement_classes.convention: Nothing executable enforces it. A named reader is responsible for verifying it.
enforcement_classes.analytical_review: A real handler enforces it, but no executable test drives that handler. A named reader verifies it by reading the handler. The four classes have no slot for enforced-but-untested; this is where those entries sit, with `handler` populated so the gap is legible.

notes_on_duplicate_claims: Several skills state the same guarantee in their own words. Each such sentence maps to exactly one entry: the entry carries the primary `skill`/`locator`, and every other sentence stating the same guarantee is listed in `also_claimed_in`. No claiming sentence found in the thirteen skills is left unmapped.
